name: Râmiz Pasha
bio: Ramiz Pasha was the Qapudan, or Lord High Admiral, and an intimate friend of Sultan Mustafa IV; after the revolution that dethroned that monarch he fled to Russia, where he wrote gazels showing how he yearned for his friend and his native land.
The poems here are taken from E. J. W. Gibb's Ottoman Poems (1882), the first English verse translations of Ottoman poetry; dates and biographical details follow Gibb's Biographical Notices.

poems.title: Although My Heart the Truth of Those Who
poems.author: Râmiz Pasha
poems.text:
Although my heart the truth of Those who wrong themselves doth show, O Lord!
In virtue of the words Do not despair, Thy love bestow, O Lord!

Beside the mead of truth and calm make aye my soul to go, O Lord!
My virtue's rose to tint and scent as captive do not throw, O Lord!

From vain attachments' stain wash pure and clean my heart as snow, O Lord!
Against me place not Thou the loathsome pool of lies of foe, O Lord!

The burning pain of exile no relief can ever know, O Lord!
Enow, if Thou the camphor-salve, the dawn of hope, did show, O Lord!

Thy slave is Râmiz; unto none save Thee doth he bend low, O Lord!
Before Thy mercy's gate his tears from eyes and eyelids flow, O Lord!
